cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The HTTP seam test imported the not-yet-created server-owned catalog configuration function.
impact: No production code was accepted as passing before the HTTP provider boundary was implemented.
lesson: Write the real HTTP consumer test before adding the application-level authority injection seam.

cause: Independent review found that the real Notebook planner still reads only the native capability manifest; the injected catalog consumer seam does not yet publish custom capability declarations to the planner.

evidence.ref: backend/workbench/http/notebook_routes.py and NotebookPlanningAgent capability catalog construction

impact: This provider-injection line proves HTTP consumption and keeps execution closed, but it does not claim real Agent discovery of custom capabilities. Planner projection is the next bounded integration line.
lesson: Keep server injection, planner projection, artifact vocabulary, and execution admission as separate verifiable seams.

cause: The first attempt to formally rescope the line for planner projection was rejected because the current CLI disallows a direct backend/workbench/app.py allowlist path as too broad.
impact: No Context Pack was modified; the planner projection was intentionally deferred to a new line instead of bypassing formal scope control.
lesson: When a frozen scope cannot be safely expanded through the formal CLI, close the bounded slice and start the next line from its exact commit rather than editing FMS records manually.

cause: The HTTP provider injection test initially failed at collection because the server-owned configuration seam did not exist yet; two subsequent fixture failures used missing context and artifact vocabulary facts before the test matched existing Notebook contracts.
impact: The red test now passes against the real HTTP route; no production behavior was accepted before the test was red and the existing context/artifact contracts were corrected.
lesson: HTTP consumer tests must use the existing context fingerprint and published artifact vocabulary before attributing failures to the provider seam.

cause: The bounded provider injection implementation passed its declared targeted regression suites and diff checks.
impact: The HTTP route consumes a server-owned catalog, emits a binding-pinned v1.2 option, rejects invalid provider configuration, and leaves the existing native lifecycle compatible. No new execution operation was added.
lesson: Accept a Notebook provider seam only with real route, compatibility, lifecycle, vocabulary, and naming evidence.

cause: The integrated quick gate reached the existing code-execution and sandbox tests, but this macOS host returned sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted.
impact: The quick gate reported 3777 passed, 20 host-containment/code-execution failures, 8 skipped, and 1 xfailed. These failures match the declared managed-host capability limitation and are not evidence against this Notebook provider slice.
lesson: Treat sandbox containment as a supported-host acceptance gate; do not convert managed-host sandbox refusal into a product regression or release pass.

cause: The declared HTTP provider-injection boundary is implemented and evidence-verified.
impact: The app can receive a trusted server-owned CapabilityBindingCatalog; Notebook HTTP requests pass it into NotebookService; v1.2 materialize-only options are consumed and reloaded across requests. Planner projection for custom capabilities, authority persistence, and automatic execution remain outside this line.
lesson: Close a narrow provider-consumer seam with explicit non-claims, then start planner projection from the exact closeout commit.
